findings.desc: Metadata filtering in active worktree overlap detection hard-codes broad roots/filenames instead of using the runtime artifact registry. It can hide material files with runtime-like basenames and treats .omx as ignored metadata despite local OMX being disabled, so real overlapping material changes can be missed.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by removing local broad metadata root/filename filters from lattice-parallel-wave.ts and routing ignored changed files through isMaterialExcludedPath, which uses story metadata and runtime artifact registry semantics. Smoke now asserts packages/main/src/process-events.jsonl remains material and .lattice runtime/story metadata remains ignored. Verified with npm --prefix packages/main run build and node packages/main/dist/tasks/lattice-parallel-wave-smoke.js.

findings.desc: Changed-file probes are collected for all active stories, but failed probe risk is only attached to selected story refs. If a selected story has no overlap while another active story has a broken registered worktree, the selected story can still be recommended parallel_dev with no visible collection-level risk.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by adding activeStoryChangedFileProbeFailures into story safety resolution. Any failed changed-file probe from another active story now adds a visible warn degradation, appears in blockers/guidance, and degrades selected output to plan_only until every active worktree projection succeeds. Smoke covers selecting B-clean while B-missing-worktree is active and broken.

findings.desc: The story-worktree smoke claims to cover relative worktree path resolution, but seeded overlap stories store absolute worktree.path values. The new assertion bypasses resolveWorktreePath relative-path behavior and would pass even if relative .worktrees/<id> handling regressed.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed smoke fixture by persisting worktree.path as relative .worktrees/<id> instead of absolute temp-root paths. The story-worktree execution assertion now exercises resolveWorktreePath relative-path fallback through git common root.

findings.desc: CHK-001 adversarial coverage requires a registered-but-missing or broken worktree to remain visible as changedFiles.status=failed with degradation and plan_only fallback. The smoke only asserts not_configured and ok statuses, so failed probe behavior is not mechanically covered.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed smoke coverage by adding B-missing-worktree with a registered but absent relative worktree path. Tests assert changedFiles.status=failed, warning degradation, plan_only recommendation, and collection-level degradation of a selected clean story when another active probe failed.
